final_proof:
Put \(a_n=\lVert v_n\rVert\). Let \(\mathcal F\) be the set of all finite subsets of \(\mathbb N=\{1,2,\ldots\}\), directed by inclusion, and, for \(F\in\mathcal F\), put
\[
A_F=\sum_{n\in F}a_n.
\]
By the definition of absolute net convergence of a generalized sum, statement (1) says precisely that the real net \((A_F)_{F\in\mathcal F}\) converges to \(r\). For \(m\ge 1\), put
\[
B_m=\sum_{n=1}^m a_n=A_{\{1,\ldots,m\}}.
\]
By the definition of absolute convergence of a series to the nonnegative real number \(r\), statement (2) says precisely that \(B_m\to r\). We prove that these two assertions are equivalent.

Suppose first that \(A_F\to r\). Given \(\varepsilon>0\), choose a finite set \(F_0\subseteq\mathbb N\) such that
\[
F\supseteq F_0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad |A_F-r|<\varepsilon.
\]
Choose \(m_0\) so large that \(F_0\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m_0\}\). If \(m\ge m_0\), then \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\supseteq F_0\), and hence
\[
|B_m-r|=|A_{\{1,\ldots,m\}}-r|<\varepsilon.
\]
Consequently \(B_m\to r\), proving (2).

Conversely, suppose that \(B_m\to r\). Since every \(a_n\ge0\), the sequence \((B_m)\) is nondecreasing. It follows that \(B_m\le r\) for every \(m\): if some \(B_m>r\), then every later partial sum would be at least \(B_m\), contradicting convergence to \(r\). Given \(\varepsilon>0\), choose \(m_0\) such that
\[
0\le r-B_{m_0}<\varepsilon.
\]
Let \(F_0=\{1,\ldots,m_0\}\), and consider any finite \(F\supseteq F_0\). Choose \(M\ge m_0\) such that \(F\subseteq\{1,\ldots,M\}\), which is possible because \(F\) is finite. Nonnegativity of the summands gives
\[
B_{m_0}=A_{F_0}\le A_F\le B_M\le r.
\]
Therefore
\[
|A_F-r|=r-A_F\le r-B_{m_0}<\varepsilon.
\]
This holds for every \(F\supseteq F_0\), so \(A_F\to r\), proving (1). Thus (1) and (2) are equivalent.

The Banach-space hypothesis is not needed for this particular equivalence between the two scalar notions of absolute convergence; it additionally guarantees that finiteness of \(\sum_n\lVert v_n\rVert\) makes the corresponding vector partial sums converge in \(V\).
